items.title: McDonald's still a tasty pick for investors, market expert says
items.summary:
STORY: McDonald's last week missed U.S. sales growth expectations for the second quarter, blaming execution lapses that blunted its value push aimed at lower-income consumers who have been cutting back restaurant spending.

The fast-food chain's shares are down more than 10% in 2026.

Still, Miller has faith that the burger giant will always find a way to bounce back.

"When you think about McDonald's and you look at the history, it's a company that actually has quietly and regularly innovated," she said. "I liken it a little bit to the arc we're going through with AI. We're asking, 'Can traditional software pivot, embrace new technology, new tastes, and move forward?' McDonald's has proven time and time again, while its reputation is for the value meal, they keep adjusting their menu to America's tastes. And I'm very confident they will continue to do that."
